title: Bellbird Bay Rising Again
premise: Lior Halloran has spent eleven years hiding in Bellbird Bay, running a struggling café and lending out pieces of their heart while keeping the whole thing locked away. When a letter lost in the mail since a decade ago surfaces—written by the person Lior loved and abandoned to protect a family secret—its sender, now-powerful developer Wren Ashcombe, returns to town with plans that would raze the waterfront, café included. As Lior fights to save both the café and the truth of why they vanished, old love curdles into open war over power, money, and who gets to rewrite Bellbird Bay's future. In the end, Lior chooses exposure over safety: they publish the family secret that once silenced them, Wren abandons the development rather than become what their ambition made them, and the two risk everything—café, reputation, and whole hearts—together.
about_author: Elodie Coldharbour is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper editor who spent years covering council meetings where love and land use collided. She writes romance about people who learn that the bravest thing you can do with a secret is stop keeping it.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Opening on a morning of burnt sugar and red-inked bank letters, Lior counts down the café's remaining weeks while serving the town that thinks it knows them. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking fear—the safe life is cracking.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Wall
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During emergency plumbing repairs, a builder pulls an envelope from behind the café's original wall paneling: postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to Lior, never delivered. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: What I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lior's POV. Eleven years earlier: young Lior and Wren Ashcombe, a summer of almosts, and the night Lior left town without goodbye after discovering their family's role in a fire that killed Wren's father. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness entangled.

chapters.title: Ashcombe Returns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren arrives in Bellbird Bay as head of Ashcombe Development, announcing a waterfront project that includes demolishing the block holding Halloran's Café. Seeing Lior across the town hall crowd stops them cold. Emotional beat: controlled fury over an old wound reopened.

chapters.title: Coffee, Bitter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks into the café to deliver the demolition notice personally and finds the lost letter's handwriting framed on Lior's wall—a copy Lior made. A brittle conversation crackles with unfinished history. Emotional beat: attraction weaponized into hostility.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior drafts and burns three replies to the letter, then throws themselves into a last-ditch plan: a heritage petition to save the building. Their grandmother's silence about the fire deepens. Emotional beat: determination born of desperation.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the council hearing, Lior speaks publicly for the first time in years; Wren, chairing, must recuse themselves but watches. The petition fails by one vote. Emotional beat: public humiliation sharpening private resolve.

chapters.title: Rain on the Breakwater
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Lior walking the storm wall at midnight; instead of gloating, they argue until arguing becomes something else—an almost-kiss interrupted by Wren's phone and the deal waiting back home. Emotional beat: longing fighting loyalty to ambition.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Going through family papers for the appeal, Lior finds evidence confirming the fire was set to cover their grandfather's debts—and that Wren's father knew and stayed silent too. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under every certainty.

chapters.title: Pieces on Loan
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's business partner pressures them to fast-track demolition before appeals stall the project. Wren hesitates, then signs anyway, telling themselves it's just business. Emotional beat: corruption beginning its quiet work.

chapters.title: One Night, No Names
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the bay's midsummer festival, Lior and Wren fall into each other deliberately, agreeing to one night without past or future. It is tender, funny, and doomed by dawn. Emotional beat: borrowed happiness, knowingly counterfeit.

chapters.title: The Morning After the Morning After
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior wakes alone to find Wren left before sunrise—and a demolition date posted on the café door. They realize the night changed nothing for Wren's plans. Emotional beat: heartbreak hardening into anger.

chapters.title: Leverage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers their partner has been bribing council members and cutting corners on asbestos reports for the site. Confronted, the partner reminds Wren how much they've already signed. Emotional beat: complicity closing like a trap.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior finally confronts their grandmother, who confesses the full truth and begs Lior to let it stay buried—for the family name, for Wren's peace. Lior refuses. Emotional beat: choosing truth over inherited shame.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With thirty days to demolition, Lior launches a public campaign using the café as community hub; Wren secretly delays paperwork to buy time, lying to their partner. They meet again as adversaries who can't stop orbiting each other. Emotional beat: love and duty pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The partner, suspecting Wren's sabotage, leaks the fire story to the press—but frames it as the Hallorans' crime alone, igniting the town against Lior. Customers vanish; the café empties. Emotional beat: betrayal upon betrayal.

chapters.title: Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cornered, Lior decides to publish everything themselves—their family's guilt and Wren's father's knowledge alike—at a packed town meeting, standing in front of Wren to do it. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into courage; invisibility ends here.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The revelation detonates: the partner's fraud unravels under scrutiny, the council inquiry reopens, and Wren, realizing what their ambition nearly cost, publicly withdraws the development and testifies against their own company. Emotional beat: climax—power renounced, truth survived.

chapters.title: Ashes and Flour
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the aftermath, Lior rebuilds the café's reputation one honest loaf at a time while grieving the family name they burned to save the truth. Wren waits outside each morning, not pushing. Emotional beat: quiet grief making room for hope.

chapters.title: Bellbird Song
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, stripped of the empire, asks for nothing except to be allowed to earn back trust—starting with helping restore the café's original wall paneling, letter and all. Emotional beat: humility as the beginning of love.

chapters.title: Rising Again
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On reopening day, the town returns; the heritage listing saves the building permanently. Lior gives Wren not pieces this time but the whole heart, and Wren offers theirs in return. Emotional beat: joy earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Postmarked at Last
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. One year later, Lior frames the original letter beside a new one—Wren's reply, written eleven years late and finally answered. The bellbirds sing over the bay. Emotional beat: completion; the past delivered, the future claimed.
